name: Apollo.io
description: Apollo.io is a B2B contact database with the outbound tools bolted on top - a 200M+ contact and company search you can filter down to a target list, then email, call and sequence those people without leaving the tab. The free plan is genuinely usable, which is why it is the default first stop for anyone doing cold outreach. The way people make money with it is not reselling the data (the terms do not allow that) - it is running outbound and appointment-setting as a paid service for clients, where two seats at $49-$79 a month replace a data vendor, a sequencing tool and a dialer that would otherwise cost several hundred. pricing_details: Apollo.io published pricing as of late 2026 is four self-serve tiers plus custom Enterprise, billed per user and metered by credits. Free (Starter) is $0 forever with no card: 900 credits a year released monthly, capped database access, basic sequences that send from Gmail only, and the Chrome extension. Basic is $49 per user/month billed annually (monthly costs more): 30,000 credits a year, Microsoft and custom mailboxes, advanced filters, limited buying-intent data, and CRM sync to HubSpot or Salesforce. Professional is $79 per user/month annual: 48,000 credits a year, the dialer with call recording, A/B testing, AI features, advanced reporting and intent data - this is the tier most outbound teams settle on. Organization is $119 per user/month annual with a three-seat minimum: 72,000 credits a year, SSO, admin controls, customizable reporting and priority support. Enterprise is a custom quote and is the only tier that permits API access and using Apollo data inside your own product. Annual billing saves up to about 24% over monthly. The seat price is only the entry ticket - data runs on credits. A verified email is roughly 1 credit, a mobile or direct-dial number roughly 8 credits, enrichment varies by activity, AI research is usage-based, and export credits burn every time contacts leave Apollo through a CSV, CRM workflow or API push. Unused credits do not roll over - they expire at the end of the billing cycle. Apollo's Fair-Use Policy caps the 'unlimited' language at 10,000 credits a month for non-paying accounts, or the lesser of (amount paid divided by $0.025) or 1M a year for paying accounts. The affiliate program pays 15% on monthly plans and 20% on annual, recurring, with a 90-day cookie.

Credits do not roll over and they vanish at the end of each billing cycle, so a plan sized for a busy month is wasted in a slow one, and heavy reveals plus exports on a small plan means buying add-on credits mid-cycle at a worse rate

It is a sales tool, not a marketing one, and it does not do content, ads or SEO - if your growth motion is inbound, Apollo solves a problem you may not have, and the per-seat price adds up fast for teams that only use it occasionally

faq.question: Is Apollo.io free, and what does the free plan actually give you?
faq.answer: Yes, there is a free-forever Starter plan with no card required. It includes 900 credits a year released monthly, capped access to the contact database, basic email sequences and the Chrome extension. The catches are that free accounts can only send from Gmail (connecting Outlook, Microsoft 365 or a custom mailbox needs a paid plan), credits are limited, and data reveals and exports are capped. For a solo founder testing whether cold outreach works, that is enough to validate the motion. For anyone sending at volume or using Outlook, Basic at $49 per user/month is the real starting point.

Second, the affiliate program pays 15% on monthly plans and 20% on annual, recurring, with a 90-day cookie, which suits anyone who writes or teaches cold email. What does not work is reselling the database - Apollo's terms bar using its data inside an external product or selling raw lists without an Enterprise agreement, and accounts that do it get closed.

content:
# Apollo.io Review 2026: The Free Lead Database That Pays for Itself (If You Use It Right)

I have built cold outreach lists in Apollo for two agencies and a couple of my own offers, and the pattern is always the same. People sign up for the free plan expecting a lead list they can sell, get a warning from support about the terms, and either quit or figure out the actual money - which is not in the data at all. It is in what you do with it.

This review covers what Apollo really is, where the money is, what it costs once you use it seriously, and the one thing that will get your account closed.

## What Apollo.io Actually Is

Apollo is two products wearing one login. The first is a B2B contact database - around 200 million contacts and tens of millions of companies - that you filter down to a target list by title, seniority, headcount, industry, tech stack, funding and hiring signals. The second is the outbound kit built on top: email and mobile reveals, sequences, A/B testing, a dialer with call recording, a Chrome extension and CRM sync to HubSpot and Salesforce.

The pitch is consolidation. Instead of paying a data vendor, a sequencing tool and a dialer separately, you do all three in one place, and the free tier lets you test the whole motion before you spend anything. That part is real, and it is why Apollo is the default first stop for anyone doing cold outreach.

The trade-off is that the seat price is only the entry ticket. Everything interesting - revealing an email, pulling a mobile number, enriching a record, pushing a contact to your CRM - runs on credits, and the credit meter is where the real cost lives.

## The Money Angle

There are two routes that hold up, and one that does not.

**1. Run outbound as a service.** This is the main one. Use Apollo to build a target list and sequence for a client, book meetings, and bill a monthly retainer - commonly $1,500 to $5,000 depending on the offer and the volume. Your cost is a couple of seats plus credits, so a few hundred revealed contacts a month is a few dollars, not a line item. One client at $2,000 a month against $79 in seats and maybe $50 in credits is the whole business case.

**2. The affiliate program.** Apollo pays 15% on monthly plans and 20% on annual, recurring, with a 90-day cookie. If you write about cold email, run a YouTube channel or send a newsletter, that is ongoing commission rather than a one-off payout - and unlike the data play below, it is fully within the terms.

**What does not work: reselling the data.** People sign up planning to build lists and sell them. Apollo's terms restrict using its contact data inside an external product or selling raw lists, and that access sits behind an Enterprise or API agreement. Accounts that try it get closed. If your idea is 'scrape Apollo, package the list, charge for it,' the idea is a terms violation, not a business.

## Pricing in 2026

Apollo's self-serve pricing is four tiers plus a custom Enterprise plan, billed per user and metered by credits.

- **Free** - $0 forever: 900 credits a year released monthly, capped database access, Gmail-only sending, the Chrome extension.
- **Basic** - $49/user/month billed annually: 30,000 credits a year, Microsoft and custom mailboxes, advanced filters, limited buying-intent data, CRM sync.
- **Professional** - $79/user/month annual: 48,000 credits, the dialer with call recording, A/B testing, AI features, advanced reporting. This is where most outbound teams land.
- **Organization** - $119/user/month annual, three-seat minimum: 72,000 credits, SSO, admin controls, priority support.
- **Enterprise** - custom quote, and the only tier that allows API access and using Apollo data inside your own product.

Annual billing saves up to about 24% over monthly. The credit meter is the part to budget for: a verified email is roughly 1 credit, a mobile or direct-dial number roughly 8, enrichment and AI research vary, and export credits burn every time contacts leave Apollo through a CSV, CRM workflow or API push. Unused credits do not roll over - they expire at the end of each cycle - and the 'unlimited' language is capped by a Fair-Use Policy at 10,000 credits a month for non-paying accounts, or the lesser of (amount paid divided by $0.025) or 1M a year for paying ones. A five-person team on Professional is about $4,740 a year in seats before a single add-on credit.

## Where It Falls Short

The first wall is data quality, and it is uneven. US tech and SaaS titles are strong. Niche industries, non-English markets and smaller companies carry stale emails and wrong numbers, and you still pay credits to reveal contacts that bounce. If your market is outside the well-covered segments, budget for a higher bounce rate and verify before you send.

The second wall is the credit model itself. Because reveals, mobiles and exports all draw down the same pool, and the pool resets rather than rolls over, a plan sized for a busy month is wasted in a slow one, and a heavy month on a small plan means buying add-ons mid-cycle at a worse rate. This is the cost that surprises people who compared only the seat prices.

The third is that Apollo is a sales tool, not a marketing one. It does not do content, ads or SEO. If your growth is inbound, you may be paying per seat for a problem you do not have - and the price stacks up quickly for teams that only reach for it occasionally.

## The Honest Verdict

Apollo is the best-value entry point into B2B prospecting right now, and the free plan is real enough to test the whole motion for nothing. If you run outbound for clients, the math is easy to like: a couple of seats and a few dollars of credits against a retainer for the meetings you book. If you write or teach in the sales space, the recurring affiliate is a clean second income. But go in clear on two things - the seat price is not the real cost, the credits are, and the data is a tool for your own outreach, not a product you can sell. Get those right and it pays for itself. Get the second one wrong and you lose the account.
